prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# 10 Stocks to Buy on January 2, 2019

**A caveat first:** I know how 2019–2023 turned out (COVID, the 2021 boom, the 2022 bear market, the AI rally). I can't truly "un-know" that, so any list I write is shaped by hindsight, whether I include the winners or leave out the losers. Below is my best attempt to use only arguments that were common in January 2019. After that, I show roughly how the picks actually did.

## The list, as of January 2, 2019

**The setting:** The S&P 500 had just fallen about 20% from its September high to its Christmas Eve low. The strategy is to buy high-quality companies with long growth runways that the selloff had marked down.

| # | Stock | Jan-2019 thesis | Key risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure is growing about 75% a year, and Office is shifting to subscriptions, which makes revenue recurring. | Cloud competition from AWS |
| 2 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | It dominates search, owns YouTube, and holds over $100B in cash. | Antitrust and privacy regulation |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS and advertising are high-margin businesses that should drive profits up sharply. | Heavy spending; high valuation |
| 4 | **Facebook (FB)** | The stock is down about 40% from its 2018 peak, at roughly 20x earnings, with 2.3B users plus Instagram and WhatsApp. | Scandals, regulation, rising costs |
| 5 | **Visa (V)** | It benefits from the long shift from cash to cards, with a toll-road model and very high margins. | Fintech disruption; fee regulation |
| 6 | **Adobe (ADBE)** | The Creative Cloud subscription model is proven, and Marketo and Magento expand its marketing software business. | Valuation |
| 7 | **Nvidia (NVDA)** | It is down about 50% on a crypto-related inventory glut, but it leads in data-center GPUs for AI training and in gaming. | Cyclical and volatile; the riskiest pick |
| 8 | **UnitedHealth (UNH)** | Its Optum unit diversifies the business, and earnings have grown steadily at double digits. | "Medicare for All" political risk |
| 9 | **Costco (COST)** | Membership fees and about 90% renewal rates make it resilient against Amazon. | Thin margins; premium valuation |
| 10 | **Boeing (BA)** | It has a record backlog of about 5,800 planes, a planned 737 production increase, and strong free cash flow and buybacks. | Execution risk; the Lion Air 737 MAX crash investigation |

## Hindsight check: what actually happened (early 2019 to end of 2023)

These are approximate price changes from memory, so please verify them before relying on them.

| Stock | Approx. price change |
|---|---|
| Nvidia | ~+1,300% (about 14x) |
| Microsoft | ~+270% |
| Costco | ~+225% |
| Facebook/Meta | ~+170% |
| Alphabet | ~+165% |
| Adobe | ~+165% |
| UnitedHealth | ~+110% |
| Amazon | ~+100% |
| Visa | ~+95% |
| Boeing | ~-20% (737 MAX groundings, then COVID) |
| **S&P 500** | **~+90% price, ~+107% with dividends** |

The equal-weighted list would have beaten the index easily, even without Nvidia.

## Why you shouldn't draw the obvious conclusion

- **This list benefits from hindsight.** Plenty of equally reasonable January 2019 lists included GE, Intel, AT&T, Kraft Heinz, Walgreens, Disney, PayPal, or Alibaba, and those lagged badly or lost money.
- **Most professionals fail at this.** S&P's SPIVA reports consistently show that a large majority of U.S. large-cap fund managers underperform the S&P 500 over five-year periods.
- **Concentration cuts both ways.** A 10-stock portfolio can beat the index by a wide margin or trail it badly. Boeing shows how a consensus "safe" pick can collapse.

If your real goal is long-term wealth rather than beating the index, a low-cost S&P 500 index fund was, and remains, the hard-to-beat default. A common compromise is to keep most of your money in index funds and a small portion in individual picks.

This is educational, not personalized investment advice.
